newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Treasury halts dollar-linked bond issues.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Treasury halts dollar-linked bond issues.

text.p: Israel's Treasury has no plans to issue dollar-linked bonds in July, the circular outlining its monthly bond auction programme shows.
"A certain series of bonds has ended and the Treasury is not opening a new series for various reasons," the Treasury said, without identifying the reasons.

The shekel plunged some five percent in the last week of June, reaching as low as 3.592 on the dollar on Friday. In the last two days, the Israeli currency has rebounded to 3.549 but analysts said on Tuesday that the market remained nervous.
The shekel fell after the Israeli cabinet approved exchange rate reforms that widened the diagonal band in which the currency may trade.

The Treasury said it would raise 1.6 bilion shekels in July -- 900 million shekels of CPI-linked bonds and 700 million shekels worth of unlinked bonds. Some of 200 million shekels of the total were already issued on the last day of June, it added.
The Treasury emphasised that the programme was based on forecasts and could change.

In June the government raised 1.6 billion shekels in the domestic capital market, of which 47.6 percent was in CPI-linked bonds, 41.5 percent in unlinked bonds and 10.9 percent in dollar-linked bonds.
